transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-07
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhou (Redwood SE), Lena Gomez (Redwood CSM), Dr. Priya Nair (Ember), Alex Romero (Ember Cloud), Samir Khan (Ember SecOps), Tina Park (Ember PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
- Scoping call for a 6-week POC to validate private networking and data residency for Ember Diagnostics.
- Success criteria: regional residency (EU + US), no egress to third-party storage, <200ms 95th latency for chat path, ability to key-manage via customer's KMS, benchmarking using 50k tokens/day nominal and scaled tests to 1.5M tokens/day.
- Proposed connectivity: PrivateLink preferred, fallback VPC peering where PrivateLink not possible; strict egress rules and explicit allowlist; plan to run end-to-end benchmarks in EU-West-1 and us-west-2.

Topics: POC scope, connectivity options (PrivateLink vs VPC peering), egress boundaries, registry/KMS integration, benchmark plan, timeline, success criteria, next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — can we do quick intros?
[00:08] Priya: Sure, I'm Priya, Head of ML at Ember. We're building diagnostics models, privacy is big for us.
[00:15] Alex: Alex, cloud eng, I'll handle networking bits.
[00:18] Samir: Samir, SecOps, curious about egress and key management.
[00:22] Maya: Awesome — Ethan from Redwood will go through the technical approach and benchmark plan. Ethan, over to you.
[00:27] Ethan: Thanks. Quick note: apologies if transcription messes up names, I thnk the call recorder sometimes flips. So the objective for today is to get enough detail to size the POC, pick connectivity, and define success criteria.
[02:12] Ethan: For connectivity we generally offer three patterns: hosted with PrivateLink into your VPC, VPC peering for fully routed networks, or private deployment if you need on-prem. For this POC PrivateLink is often the quickest for strict egress controls because traffic doesn't traverse internet gateways.
[03:05] Alex: For us PrivateLink is preferred but we need to confirm whether our cloud provider supports cross-account endpoints in EU region. Also we have firewall rules that block outbound except to allowlist.
[03:22] Ethan: That's fine, PrivateLink will sit behind your NLB and we only require specific IP ranges for health checks, which we can keep minimal. For peering you get routable access, but peering means more ops on your side.
[04:10] Priya: On success criteria — our product team wants model responses for triage prompts within 150ms p95 ideally, but we can accept up to 200ms for worst-case. We also need embeddings latency under 250ms for the small batch job.
[04:34] Ethan: Ok noted. For the POC we should instrument both token-level latency and end-to-end request latency. We'll provide a benchmark harness that hits the exact prompt set.
[05:01] Tina: Timeline question — how long to prove this?
[05:07] Maya: We typically run a 4–6 week POC: week 0 prep, week 1 connectivity & smoke tests, weeks 2–3 benchmarks and tuning, week 4 sign-off. If PrivateLink has approvals it can add a week.
[05:20] Samir: Approvals are the sticky part. We'll need SOC 2 details, encryption at rest/in transit, and ability to use our KMS for model payload keys or at least envelope encryption.
[05:35] Ethan: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; for hosted we support envelope encryption with bring-your-own-key integrations in the PrivateLink flow — we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[06:00] Alex: We also want to ensure no logs or payloads leave the region, and no third-party log aggregation.
[06:08] Lena: We'll provide retention controls and audit logs — I'll highlight that in the docs we send.
[06:20] Ethan: For the benchmark sizing, what's your expected workload? Priya?
[06:28] Priya: Typical: 10k inference requests/day for triage chat, average prompt+response ~350 tokens, peaks up to 10 RPS sustained during business hours. We also run nightly embedding batches: roughly 50k items, 512-dim embeddings. For POC we'd like to scale synthetic load to emulate 100k requests/day and up to 1.5M tokens/day to test auto-scaling.
[06:58] Ethan: Good. That gives us token counts and qps. We'll suggest three model profiles for POC: small latency-optimized, medium cost-balanced, and a quantized high-throughput variant if you want to stress cost. Each will have cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated.
[07:22] Priya: Can you explain 'dedicated' a bit — what does that buy us for latency vs hosted?
[07:29] Ethan: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity so tail latency is lower and throughput predictable—less noisy neighbors. Hosted can still hit SLOs but with autoscaling; dedicated is preferred when you need strict 95/99 p95 tails and constant high QPS. For POC we usually start hosted + PrivateLink then move to dedicated if the numbers require it.
[08:05] Alex: For PrivateLink we need specific IPs to allow — can you provide those ranges?
[08:12] Maya: We'll provide a minimal set; there's also a path with VPC peering where you control all route tables. For peering you need to coordinate route advertisement and ensure no overlapping CIDRs.
[08:33] Samir: Egress constraints: we cannot allow egress to third-party storage, and logs must be kept in-region. Will Redwood persist prompts or inputs?
[08:45] Ethan: By default hosted endpoints do ephemeral caching for KV cache performance — but we can disable persistent retention or ensure data doesn't leave the VPC when using PrivateLink. We'll also provide an option to scrub PII in-flight but that'll add latency.
[09:10] Priya: We need to confirm token-level billing/usage and whether tokenization is deterministic vs any redaction changes tokens.
[09:20] Ethan: Tokenization is deterministic given the model tokenizer; the benchmark harness will use the same tokenizer as the model.
[09:30] Tina: Benchmarks — what does Redwood provide out-of-the-box?
[09:35] Ethan: We provide a JMeter/go-based harness, a set of prompts for chat and embeddings, and scripts to capture p95/p99 and token throughput. We'll also supply a spreadsheet template for success criteria so you can sign off.
[10:05] Priya: On region placement, we need EU-West-1 primarily and US-West-2 second. Is model parity across regions guaranteed?
[10:13] Ethan: We maintain the same model catalog across regions but there can be model variants and quantized builds that differ slightly in perf. We'll map model versions to region builds in the runbook.
[10:30] Alex: Other nit — our network team requires mTLS between our NLB and PrivateLink endpoints. Does Redwood support mTLS?
[10:36] Ethan: We support mTLS termination on the endpoint side, yes — we can share the TLS requirements doc.
[11:02] Samir: Audit logs — we need immutable logs of admin actions and token-level usage for 90 days.
[11:09] Lena: Our console exports audit trails; for POC we can provide a 90-day retention snapshot and an export process.
[11:20] Priya: For success criteria, summarizing: 1) residency in EU and no cross-region egress; 2) latency p95 < 200ms (target 150ms); 3) embeddings batch throughput meets nightly SLA; 4) encryption with our KMS or approved envelope; 5) bench results reproducible and documented. Agree?
[11:46] Maya: Yep. Any additions?
[11:50] Alex: Add 'no logs to third party' and 'NLB + PrivateLink mTLS' as requirements.
[11:58] Maya: Noted.
[12:10] Ethan: On benchmarking specifics, we'll run three phases: smoke (connectivity + single-request correctness), baseline (low QPS, collect p50/p95/p99), and scale (ramp to 10–15 RPS sustained and spike tests). We'll capture token counts, cold-starts, KV cache hit rate.
[12:40] Priya: KV cache — we rely on prefix cache for conversation state. If session affinity is needed, can we pin to a backend?
[12:49] Ethan: We can provide session affinity via a sticky header or through routing keys; we'll outline that in the runbook. Pinning has trade-offs on capacity.
[13:05] Tina: For orchestration who signs off on the final runbook?
[13:09] Priya: I'll own sign-off for ML; Alex will do the network sign-off; Samir for security.
[13:15] Maya: Great. We'll prepare the runbook and send it as part of the POC kickoff package.
[13:30] Alex: Regarding IP allowlist — do you use a fixed set for PrivateLink or will they be ephemeral?
[13:37] Ethan: PrivateLink endpoints are within your VPC, the external egress we ask to allow is small for health checks; we'll provide fixed ranges for the duration of the POC. For hosted public endpoints ranges can be broader.
[14:05] Priya: Cost — can you give a rough hosted vs dedicated for our scale?
[14:12] Ethan: For the baseline numbers you cited (10k req/day, 350 tokens avg) hosted is typically lower up-front; dedicated becomes cost-effective above sustained high QPS, e.g., >50 RPS sustained or heavy embedding batch workloads. We'll run cost models and include quantized variants that reduce memory/compute by ~40-60% with small quality regressions.
[14:40] Maya: We'll include a cost worksheet for three scenarios.
[15:00] Tina: Any compliance docs we need to see right away?
[15:04] Samir: SOC 2 plus data processing agreement and encryption details.
[15:08] Maya: We'll share SOC 2 report and DPA; Ethan will add KMS integration notes.
[15:18] Ethan: For in-region storage, we can configure logs to stream to a regional S3 under your account via PrivateLink, no third-party hops.
[15:30] Priya: Good. On metrics, we want to capture qualitative model quality — we will run evaluation prompts and expect no more than X% degradation vs current baseline.
[15:41] Ethan: Add that to success criteria — quality thresholds per prompt set. We'll support automated evals as part of the harness.
[16:00] Alex: For the POC environment, will you provide test accounts or do we set up our own?
[16:06] Maya: We'll provision a POC tenant with restricted capacities and keys; you can choose to bring own keys for envelope.
[16:14] Priya: Are there rate limits we'll hit during the scale tests?
[16:18] Ethan: We'll lift default rate limits for the POC to allow the ramp; we just need a heads up on the planned traffic windows.
[16:33] Tina: Let's capture the proposed POC timeline and milestones.
[16:37] Maya: Week 0 (2026-05-18): Kickoff + runbook finalized. Week 1 (2026-05-25): Connectivity + smoke tests. Week 2-3: Baseline benchmarking and tuning. Week 4: Scale tests + quality eval. Week 5: Sign-off and handoff. We can compress if approvals are fast.
[17:02] Priya: That works.
[17:10] Alex: For metrics we'll need dashboards — can Redwood hook into our Datadog or do you provide an export?
[17:16] Ethan: We can stream metrics into Datadog via a private forwarder in your account or provide CSV exports; Datadog integration requires an agent in-region, we'll add that to the runbook.
[17:30] Samir: Last question — if we see a quality regression after we go to a quantized model, is there an automatic fallback to the full-precision model?
[17:37] Ethan: Yes, our routing supports canary rollbacks and auto-fallback policies; the console can trigger failover to a golden model.
[17:50] Priya: Great.
[18:00] Maya: Ok let's recap action items and next steps.
[18:05] Maya: Action recap: 1) Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS + PrivateLink runbook; 2) Redwood to share benchmark harness and cost worksheet; 3) Ember to share target regions, IP allowlist, contact for network approvals; 4) Schedule kickoff for week of 2026-05-18.
[18:28] Priya: We'll aim to have internal sign-offs by 2026-05-12.
[18:35] Maya: Perfect — any final questions?
[18:40] Tina: None from my side.
[18:44] Samir: No.
[18:47] Alex: All good.
[18:50] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with docs and proposed kickoff times.
[18:55] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker mislabels and dropped words; numbers double-checked in action items above.
